description: Retrieve saved filter dimensions for a datasource.

examples.user_query: What dimensions are available for the SalesData datasource?
examples.notes: This call retrieves the saved filter dimensions for the datasource identified as 'SalesData'. Use this when you know the datasource title but not the full name.

examples.user_query: Can you list the dimensions for the datasource hosted at localhost/MyModel?
examples.notes: This call fetches dimensions for the datasource using its full name 'localhost/MyModel'. Use this when the full name is available and preferred for identification.

examples.user_query: I need the dimensions for the datasource named 'MarketingAnalytics' hosted at localhost/MarketingModel.
examples.notes: This call retrieves dimensions for the datasource using both its title ('MarketingAnalytics') and full name ('localhost/MarketingModel'). Use this when both identifiers are available for more precise querying.

description: Retrieve saved formula measures for a datasource.

examples.user_query: What are the formula measures available for the SalesData datasource?
examples.notes: This retrieves all saved formula measures for the datasource identified as 'SalesData'. Useful for understanding the calculated fields in this specific datamodel.

examples.user_query: Can you list the measures for the datasource hosted at localhost/MyModel?
examples.notes: This fetches the formula measures for the datasource with the full name 'localhost/MyModel'. Use this when you know the full path to the datasource.

examples.user_query: I need to see the measures for the datasource named 'FinanceModel' located at 'server123/FinanceModel'.
examples.notes: This retrieves formula measures for a datasource using both its identifier ('FinanceModel') and its full name ('server123/FinanceModel'). Providing both parameters can help ensure the correct datasource is queried.

description: Retrieve all datasources visible to the authenticated user.

examples.user_query: What datasources can I access in Sisense?
examples.notes: This call retrieves a list of all datasources visible to the authenticated user. Useful for understanding available data connections.

examples.user_query: Show me all the datasources I have permission to view.
examples.notes: This call returns all datasources the user is authorized to see. Ideal for auditing or exploring data access.

examples.user_query: List all datasources available in the system for my account.
examples.notes: This retrieves the full list of datasources accessible to the current user. Helpful for identifying data sources for dashboard creation.
